levelMapping: Software hiring in India is mostly the former VMware org (now the VCF division + Tanzu/NSX/vSAN teams) plus Symantec/CA/Brocade and semiconductor-firmware units. Legacy VMware ladder still used in postings/offers: MTS-1 (P1, 0-2 YOE) -> MTS-2 (P2, ~2-4 YOE) -> MTS-3 (P3, ~3-6 YOE; ≈ Google L4 / Amazon SDE II) -> SMTS / Staff (P4/P5, 6-10+ YOE; one Blind commenter maps SMTS to Google L4, so MTS-3 may sit at the L4 floor) -> Staff 2 (P6). Broadcom's own ladder appears in newer offers as IC-3/IC-4/IC-5 (a 9-YOE VCF offer in 2025 was IC-4). For ~3.3 YOE expect MTS-2 or MTS-3 depending on the bar you clear — MTS-3 Bengaluru offers reported at 49-52 LPA (2022-2024, 2.5-7 YOE), MTS-2 at ~28-33 LPA (2022-2023, 1.8-2.8 YOE). Level is often decided after the loop, so ask the recruiter which band the req is open at.

process.summary: The VMware-by-Broadcom loop in India is a 4-6 round, mostly virtual, engineer-driven process: recruiter/hiring-manager call, sometimes a 60-90 min HackerRank OA, then 2-3 one-hour technical rounds that each mix 1-2 LeetCode easy/medium problems with CS-fundamentals and language-internals questions (OS, networking, C++/Java internals), a design round (HLD for everyone, a separate LLD round for SMTS), an optional scenario/debugging round, and a hiring-manager behavioral round. Problems are rarely LC-hard; interviewers care more about clean, compiled-in-head code, edge cases and your ability to explain why (vector internals, how a mutex works, deadlock mitigation). Legacy Broadcom units (Brocade, firmware, Symantec) run shorter, more C/OS-heavy and resume-driven loops, sometimes with a written C test at an in-person drive.

rounds.name: Recruiter / hiring-manager intro call
rounds.what: Background, current project, why VMware/Broadcom, role and location (5-day WFO) expectations. Many HM calls are technical: core Java/C++ or multithreading questions and sometimes one coding problem (Trapping Rain Water was asked in an HM screen).
rounds.probes: Depth on your current project's architecture, pain points and what you would redesign; language you will code in (C/C++ for vSphere/ESXi/kernel teams, Java/Go for VCF/Tanzu/Aria control planes, Python for automation/tooling).

rounds.name: Online assessment (team-dependent)
rounds.what: HackerRank (occasionally Codility/HirePro). Typical: 2-3 coding problems (LC easy/medium: tree diameter, consecutive-numbers sum, sort-by-popcount, prefix-count problems) plus 6-15 MCQs on OS/networking/DBMS/C. Efficient solutions earn extra points; proctored with camera and tab-switch detection in 2025 reports.
rounds.probes: Hidden test cases and time/space complexity; MCQs lean GATE-style (paging, deadlock, TCP, SQL).

rounds.name: Technical round 1 - DSA + fundamentals
rounds.what: HackerRank CodePair / shared editor (often no autocomplete, no run button). Intro + 10-15 min project discussion, then 1-2 problems: linked lists (reverse, loop detect+remove, remove duplicates, middle, k-group), arrays/strings (merge sorted, anagrams, K-distinct substring), trees (LCA, invert without recursion, level order). Follow-up rapid-fire on stack vs heap, vector internals, list vs array traversal cost.
rounds.probes: Iterative AND recursive versions; constant-space constraint; complexity of each step; dry-run on an edge case (empty, single node, cycle); they expect code that would compile without a run button.

rounds.name: Technical round 2 - coding + language/OS internals
rounds.what: Second LC easy/medium set (DP such as LIS/edit-distance variants, BFS/DFS islands, kth largest, stock span, task-scheduler-like) plus a long verbal block: C++ virtual functions/vptr, diamond problem, how a mutex/spinlock/semaphore is implemented, deadlock examples and mitigation, fork and process vs thread, virtual memory/page faults/TLB, TCP vs UDP, HTTP vs HTTPS. Java teams ask ConcurrentHashMap, BlockingQueue, Thread vs Runnable, immutability.
rounds.probes: Interviewers deliberately challenge syntax and ask confusing follow-ups to test confidence; be ready to write a comparator, a thread-safe singleton or a two-thread lock on the spot.

rounds.name: Design round (HLD; SMTS gets a separate LLD round)
rounds.what: Systems-flavoured design: thread-pool library, memory-management subsystem, rolling upgrade of servers in a distributed system, job/machine (cluster) scheduler, load balancer + LRU cache, logging framework with levels, telemetry ingestion, blob-storage API. Often starts with an LRU cache implementation or vertical vs horizontal scaling / caching / master-slave warm-ups and then goes deep on failure handling.
rounds.probes: Bottlenecks and failure at each stage, consistency, SPOF avoidance, consistent hashing, sharding of your own project's DB, how your design would have survived the 2018 GitHub DDoS.

rounds.name: Scenario / debugging round (some teams)
rounds.what: Debug a C++ program that compiles but produces wrong output; GDB/WinDbg usage; how you debug running production services; log levels and reconstructing an incident from logs; how snapshots are implemented; Pune C++/kernel teams also discuss your debugging habits and tools.
rounds.probes: Systematic narrowing (bisect, breakpoints, core dumps), memory errors (dangling pointer, UB, off-by-one), reading crash dumps.

rounds.name: Hiring manager / behavioral
rounds.what: Scenario-based behavioral: conflict with teammate/manager, handling negative feedback, proudest moment, pressure and deadlines, working on an old tech stack, customer-facing escalation scenario (SMTS). Also discussion of the team's tech stack and your language comfort (e.g., rate your Java 1-10).
rounds.probes: Why leave current job; ownership stories; whether you will cope with 5-day office and a lean, high-expectation culture.

rounds.name: HR / offer
rounds.what: Expected CTC, notice period, 5-year view. Offers = base + 12% target bonus + 4-year RSU grant (quarterly vest) + joining/relocation bonus; RSU grant size is usually declared non-negotiable, cash via joining bonus is the lever. Reqs can sit 'pending budget approval' after a positive loop.

process.indiaNotes: Bengaluru is the main hub (VCF/vSphere/ESXi, vSAN, NSX, Aria/automation, Tanzu, Symantec, Brocade, semis firmware); Pune hosts C++/Windows-kernel, EUC-legacy and some Tanzu/Spring teams; Hyderabad has Symantec/CA-style Java/microservices teams. Rounds are all virtual (Zoom + HackerRank CodePair) and usually spread over 1-3 weeks, sometimes two rounds back-to-back on one day. India loops lean harder on CS fundamentals and language internals than US loops (US reports: Codility phone screen + 2 coding + 1 design + HM, more LC-medium focused). Legacy Broadcom units in Bengaluru still run in-person drives: a 20-question written C paper (syntax errors, DS, networking, OS, architecture, debugging) followed by F2F technical rounds; Brocade F2F rounds are 'very basic C' and resume-driven. EUC (Workspace ONE/Horizon) was carved out to Omnissa (KKR) in 2024 and Carbon Black folded into Symantec, so those are no longer Broadcom reqs. 5-day work-from-office is mandatory in India; attendance is tracked.
process.timeline: Glassdoor averages 14 days (Broadcom) to 18-26 days (VMware); real India reports range from 5 days (two rounds a day) to ~4 weeks, with offers arriving 2 days to 1 month after the last round. Some reqs stall after a positive loop for budget approval; 2023-2024 reports of positions put 'on hold' after final rounds and stack-ranking between finalists.
tips: Prepare linked-list and tree problems to the point of writing them iteratively and recursively without a run button; they appear in nearly every India report (reverse, loop detect+remove, remove duplicates, middle, k-group, LCA, invert without recursion).

For every data structure you use, be able to explain its internals and complexity (vector growth, hash table buckets/collisions, list vs array cache behaviour) — these follow-ups decide the round as much as the problem.

Revise OS/concurrency fundamentals as interview questions, not trivia: mutex vs semaphore vs spinlock and how a mutex is implemented, deadlock example + mitigation, process vs thread and fork(), virtual memory/page fault/TLB, what malloc does across user/kernel.

Expect C++ depth if the team is vSphere/ESXi/NSX/kernel (virtual functions, vptr, diamond problem, name mangling, extern "C", RAII); Java/Go depth for VCF control plane/Tanzu/Aria (ConcurrentHashMap, BlockingQueue, immutability, goroutines/channels).

Design rounds are infra-flavoured: practise thread pool, cluster/job scheduler, memory manager, rolling upgrades, logging/telemetry pipelines, load balancer with consistent hashing, and be ready to start by implementing an LRU cache.

Drive the project discussion yourself: flow diagram, resiliency, scale numbers, pain points and what you would redesign — several loops (SDE-4 2025, MTS-3 2021) used this as the de-facto design round.
Interviewers may argue syntax or interrupt; stay calm, state assumptions, say 'I don't know' instead of guessing (reported as appreciated).
Confirm the business unit, level band and whether the req is funded before investing in the loop; ask about layoffs in that team and the 5-day WFO policy.
If you get a take-home (Windows/kernel or Tanzu pairing teams), expect to defend it line-by-line in a later round.
process.notes: No fixed 'bar raiser' or values round; the hiring manager decides with interviewer feedback (US reports mention a hiring-committee-style review). Coding language is free in most teams, but C/C++ is expected for ESXi/kernel/Brocade/firmware roles and Java/Go for control-plane teams. Platforms: HackerRank (OA + CodePair), occasionally Codility or HirePro; interviews on Zoom. Some teams use a one-week take-home (e.g., a Windows Unicode wrapper for a kernel team) or a 3-hour case study (class diagram + pseudocode). A dedicated LLD/OOD round exists mainly at SMTS and in Symantec/CA/EUC-legacy Java teams (pub-sub, rate limiter, parking lot, in-memory game module, immutable class); for MTS-2/MTS-3 LLD questions are folded into coding or design rounds. Post-acquisition reputation (2024-2026): ~19k VMware roles cut since Nov 2023 (Heise via KORE1), repeated RIF cycles in the VCF division, mandatory 5-day office with attendance tracking in India, benefits trimmed, but strong RSU refreshers (reported India grants ~$60k SDE2 to ~$200k SDE4 over 4 years, alternating years) and pay that can exceed Google for senior ICs. Units still hiring software engineers in India in 2025-2026: VCF (vSphere/ESXi, vSAN, NSX, Aria/automation, VCF operations), parts of Tanzu, Symantec/CA infra-software (Agile Ops/Rally, mainframe, security), Brocade storage networking (C), and semiconductor firmware/validation (C/embedded). Glassdoor-wide: 'average' difficulty, 'very positive' experience, 41% applied online, 22% referral.

dsa.title: Reverse a Linked List (iterative + recursive)
dsa.variant: Asked both iteratively and recursively in one go; C teams want linear time / constant space and a whiteboard dry-run; also appears as a warm-up in firmware/Brocade rounds.
dsa.evidence: Reported in 6+ loops: Bengaluru SWE (Glassdoor, May 2022 posted Oct 2024), Bengaluru SWE in C (Taro Jul 2023), MTS-3 Feb 2022, Sr MTS 2020 round 3, Principal Bengaluru 2017, Firmware whiteboard Jun 2026

dsa.title: Detect and remove a loop in a linked list
dsa.variant: Floyd's cycle detection, then the follow-up is always 'now remove the loop' and state time/space complexity.
dsa.evidence: SMTS Bengaluru Jul 2024 round 2; GFG 2023 technical round; MTS-1 off-campus 2021 round 2; GFG VMware prep list

dsa.title: Remove duplicates from a linked list (sorted and unsorted)
dsa.variant: Unsorted variant (hash set, or O(n^2) with O(1) space) is what SMTS/Staff loops asked; Staff 2021 phrased it as 'find duplicate in linked list'.
dsa.evidence: SMTS Bengaluru Jul 2024 round 1; Broadcom Staff SWE India 2021; Interview Query Symantec reports 2024-2026

dsa.title: Middle of the Linked List (one traversal) + circular / doubly variants
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: middle of a circular list, middle of a doubly linked list, and justify the complexity of the slow/fast approach.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bengaluru Mar 2022 round 2; MTS-3 Bengaluru Jun 2021 (Glassdoor); Broadcom Plano Oct 2025 (one traversal)

dsa.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
dsa.variant: Asked after a resume deep-dive in a projects+coding round; GFG prep list also lists 'reverse a linked list in groups of given size'.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bangalore loop (LeetCode Discuss); GFG VMware preparation list

dsa.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree (nodes may be absent)
dsa.variant: Clarify whether both nodes are guaranteed present; the phone-screen version became LC 1644 (two-pass existence check vs single-pass with counters). Interviewer then asked for hardcoded test trees run live in Codility.
dsa.evidence: VMware senior phone screen (Codility); MTS-3 Bangalore round 3 'variation of LCA'; MTS-2 round 2

dsa.title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays, then Merge k Sorted Lists
dsa.variant: Round starts with LC 88 (merge sorted array in place) and escalates to LC 23 coded live; followed by stack-vs-heap and vector questions.
dsa.evidence: MTS2 Bengaluru Jan 2023 round 1

dsa.title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
dsa.variant: Asked in the coding+design round before the LRU/scaling discussion.
dsa.evidence: MTS2 Bengaluru Jan 2023 round 2

dsa.title: Group Anagrams
dsa.variant: Phrased as 'rearrange an array of strings so anagrams are adjacent'; discuss sorted-key vs count-key hashing.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bengaluru Mar 2022 round 1; GFG on-campus technical round

dsa.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (DP, then recursive formulation)
dsa.variant: Interviewer asked for the O(n^2) DP first, then to re-express it recursively (memoised); be ready for the O(n log n) patience-sorting version.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bengaluru Mar 2022 round 1; 'a DP problem' is the most common description of SMTS coding rounds (Glassdoor Dec 2023, Taro Nov 2025)

dsa.title: Min Stack + Score of Parentheses (phone-screen pair)
dsa.variant: Asked together in one 45-min phone screen; Score of Parentheses is LC 856. Plain balanced-parentheses (LC 20) is the warm-up in other loops.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bangalore phone screen; MTS-3 Mar 2022 round 2 (balanced parentheses)

dsa.title: Online Stock Span
dsa.variant: Asked as the classic 'stock span problem' on HackerRank CodePair.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bangalore Feb 2022 round 1

dsa.title: Minimum insertions and deletions to convert string A into B
dsa.variant: Reduce to LCS: deletions = |A| - LCS, insertions = |B| - LCS; interviewer may push toward full edit distance (LC 72).
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bangalore Feb 2022 round 1

dsa.title: Number of Islands (+ DFS on adjacency list with topological-order follow-up)
dsa.variant: 4-connected grid version; a separate loop asked plain DFS over an adjacency list and then 'maintain precedence order' (hint toward topological sort, LC 210). Graph DFS/BFS also cited in a Bengaluru Sr SWE 2023 loop.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bangalore Feb 2022 round 2; MTS-1 on-campus 2021 round 2; VMware Sr SWE Bengaluru Jun 2023 (Glassdoor)

dsa.title: Kth Largest Element in an array / in an infinite stream
dsa.variant: Stream version (LC 703): first 'max element in an infinite stream', then 'kth largest in the same stream' — expect to defend a min-heap of size k vs quickselect.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bangalore Feb 2022 round 3; Sr MTS Apr 2020 round 1

dsa.title: Trapping Rain Water
dsa.variant: Asked inside the hiring-manager screening call after core Java/multithreading questions.
dsa.evidence: MTS2 Bangalore Apr 2022 round 1

dsa.title: Height of a binary tree, then print its top view
dsa.statement: Given a binary tree, first return its height (LC 104). Then print the 'top view': for each horizontal distance from the root, the first node seen when looking from above. Solve with BFS carrying (node, hd) and record the first node per hd; discuss why DFS needs depth tracking to be correct.
dsa.evidence: MTS2 Bangalore Apr 2022 round 2 (after project discussion)

dsa.title: Longest substring with no two adjacent characters equal
dsa.statement: Given a string, return the longest contiguous substring in which no two neighbouring characters are the same (e.g. 'aabcbd' -> 'abcbd'). Single pass: extend while s[i] != s[i-1], reset the window start when they match; return the best window.
dsa.evidence: MTS2 Bangalore Apr 2022 round 4

dsa.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
dsa.evidence: MTS2 Bangalore Apr 2022 round 4

dsa.title: Implement a growable stack / queue / stack using queues
dsa.statement: Write a Stack class over a raw array that doubles its internal array when capacity is reached (push/pop/peek, amortised O(1)); separately, implement a queue from scratch and a stack using queues. Interviewers probe amortised analysis, shrinking policy and thread-safety of the class.
dsa.variant: SMTS round 1 asked the auto-extending stack in C++; MTS2 2022 asked 'implement a queue'; GFG 2021 asked stack via queues.
dsa.evidence: SMTS Bengaluru Jul 2024 round 1; MTS2 Apr 2022 round 4; Intern+MTS 2021 manager round

dsa.title: Design an O(1) collection: ordered, duplicates allowed, O(1) get/remove
dsa.statement: Design a list-like data structure in Java/C++ that preserves insertion order, allows duplicate values, and supports get and remove in O(1). Expected answer: a doubly linked list for order plus a hash map from value to a set/list of node references (compare with LC 380/381 Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)). A Pune 2024 variant was simply 'support these operations in O(1)' solved with hashmap + list.
dsa.evidence: MTS2 Bangalore Apr 2022 round 5 (candidate could not solve); MTS-2 Pune 2024 round 2

dsa.title: Task Scheduler (cooldown between same tasks)
dsa.variant: Reported as 'similar to Task Scheduler'; the interviewer pressed on writing a custom comparator in C++ for the heap.
dsa.evidence: VMware SMTS Nov 2023 (Glassdoor)

dsa.title: Maximum j - i such that arr[i] <= arr[j]
dsa.statement: Given an integer array, find the maximum index difference j - i with arr[i] <= arr[j] (0 if none). Brute force O(n^2) was accepted first, then the interviewer required O(n): build a prefix-min array and a suffix-max array and sweep both with two pointers. Also on GFG's VMware 'hard' list.
dsa.evidence: VMware Staff Engineer Bengaluru May 2023 (Glassdoor) coding round; GFG VMware topics list

dsa.title: Sort an array of 0s and 1s (and 0/1/2 - Sort Colors)
dsa.variant: Asked as a 10-minute warm-up before OS questions; expect one-pass Dutch-national-flag partitioning.
dsa.evidence: Sr MTS Apr 2020 round 1; Staff Engineer Jan 2021 (Glassdoor)

dsa.title: Maximum Subarray with start and end indices
dsa.variant: Kadane's with index tracking; also reported in a Broadcom-tagged practice set.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Bengaluru Jun 2021 (Glassdoor); interviewsolver Broadcom set

dsa.title: Pythagorean triple in an array (3Sum family)
dsa.statement: Given an integer array, decide whether it contains a, b, c with a^2 + b^2 = c^2. Square everything, sort, then for each candidate c^2 run a two-pointer pair-sum (O(n^2)); mention the hash-set alternative and the 3Sum / triplet-sum variants that other VMware loops asked.
dsa.variant: Plain 3Sum and 'closest 3-sum to target' (LC 16) reported in older VMware rounds; a triplet-sum variant where the interviewer graded code structure over the answer.
dsa.evidence: Broadcom SWE Sep 2026 (Glassdoor, Israel); VMware on-campus 2021 (3Sum); MTS-1 on-campus 2021 (triplet variant); VMware MTS 2017 (3-sum closest)

dsa.title: Binary search variants: first/last occurrence, rotation count
dsa.variant: Interviewers push from linear scan -> binary search + linear expansion (rejected, not O(log n)) -> two separate binary searches. A sibling question: number of rotations of a sorted rotated array = index of the minimum (LC 153).
dsa.evidence: VMware MTS on-campus (takeUforward) round 2; VMware on-campus 2021 round 2 (rotations)

dsa.title: First Missing Positive (constant space) + two missing numbers in linear time
dsa.variant: Round began with 'find the two missing numbers from 1..n in O(n)' (sum/sum-of-squares or XOR partitioning — interviewer had not seen the XOR trick), then 'smallest missing positive in an unsorted array, constant extra space' (index-marking / cyclic sort).
dsa.evidence: VMware MTS on-campus round 1 (GFG), 2 interviewers at MTS-3 level

dsa.title: Invert / mirror a binary tree without recursion (+ level-order variants)
dsa.variant: Always 'without recursion' (explicit stack or queue). Companion asks: level-order traversal, bottom-up level order / 'leaf to root nodes by level' (LC 107), swap left and right subtrees.
dsa.evidence: MTS-2 round 2 (LeetCode Discuss); Intern+MTS 2021 round 2; GFG 2023 technical round; MTS-3 Mar 2022 design round (leaf-to-root by level)

dsa.title: HackerRank OA set (MTS-2): Diameter of Binary Tree, Consecutive Numbers Sum, custom exception
dsa.variant: 90-minute HackerRank with three parts: raise and handle a custom exception in Python, LC 829 Consecutive Numbers Sum, LC 543 Diameter of Binary Tree.
dsa.evidence: VMware MTS-2 OA (LeetCode Discuss)

dsa.title: Validate BST, then merge two BSTs into one BST in O(m+n)
dsa.variant: Follow-up (explain, no code): inorder both trees to sorted lists, merge, build a balanced BST from the sorted array (LC 108) — O(m+n) time. 'BST' is also the topic named in a Nov 2025 India SWE loop.
dsa.evidence: Intern+MTS 2021 round 2 (validate BST); VMware MTS on-campus round 2 (merge BSTs); Broadcom SWE India Nov 2025 (BST + DP topics)

dsa.title: Count Negative Numbers in a Sorted Matrix
dsa.variant: Interviewer rejected the first two approaches and wanted the staircase O(m+n) walk from the top-right/bottom-left corner.
dsa.evidence: VMware on-campus 2022 technical round 2 (GFG)

dsa.title: Design a HashMap class with collision handling
dsa.variant: Discuss chaining vs open addressing before coding insert/get; the same loop series asks 'how is a hash table implemented internally' verbally (SMTS 2024).
dsa.evidence: MTS-1 2022 round 1 (20-30 min design + code); SMTS Jul 2024 round 2 (verbal)

dsa.title: Implement a vector class (push_back, shrink_to_fit) with calloc/realloc
dsa.statement: Write a minimal std::vector in C/C++: raw buffer, size and capacity, push_back with geometric growth (realloc), shrink_to_fit, operator[]; explain amortised O(1) and why constant-time indexing holds. The verbal twin — 'what is a vector and how is it implemented internally' — recurs in C++ rounds.
dsa.evidence: Intern+MTS 2021 round 1 (coded); MTS2 Jan 2023 (advantages of vector); SMTS Jul 2024 (verbal internals)

dsa.title: C bit-manipulation and memory-layout drills (Broadcom hardware/firmware units)
dsa.statement: A cluster of C questions from Broadcom (non-VMware) rounds: (1) compute sizeof a struct {int; char; short; char; int} with padding (answer 16); (2) set all bits from position start to end of an integer without a loop by building a mask ((1<<end)-1) ^ ((1<<(start-1))-1) and OR-ing; (3) 265 switches all off, toggle every 2nd/3rd/5th/7th/13th — count how many are on; (4) swap two ints without a temp or arithmetic (XOR); (5) write your own sizeof() using pointer arithmetic.
dsa.variant: Bit manipulation + pointers + linked lists was the stated syllabus of a 2023 Bengaluru SWE loop in C.
dsa.evidence: Broadcom round-1 questions post (LeetCode Discuss); Intern+MTS 2021 round 2; Broadcom SWE Bengaluru Jul 2023 (Taro)

dsa.title: Trie + DFS hard problem (Word Search II style)
dsa.variant: Reported as 'a hard-tagged LeetCode problem needing a Trie with DFS' in a 1-hour staff-level round after 20 min of project talk; candidate ran out of time and was asked to at least implement the Trie. Exact problem not named.
dsa.evidence: Blind, VMware VCDR staff interview thread (comment)

dsa.title: HackerRank OA set (2025): Sort by popcount, distinct-digit counts, permutation subarrays
dsa.statement: Three problems in a 90-min proctored HackerRank (6 MCQ + 3 coding): (1) Cardinality sorting = LC 1356; (2) for up to 1e5 queries [n, m] with m <= 1e6, count numbers whose digits are all distinct — precompute a prefix count; (3) given a permutation p of 1..n, for each k output 1 if some length-k window is a permutation of 1..k — track the span of positions of values 1..k.
dsa.evidence: linkjob.ai first-person VMware OA account, Nov 2025 (promotional site; unverified)

dsa.title: Sorting implementations and custom comparators
dsa.statement: Be ready to hand-write merge sort / quicksort / bubble sort with complexity, compare merge vs quick, and to sort with custom keys: sort a list of words alphabetically (including 'VMware') and return the second-to-last; sort an array of date strings ascending; sort a list without built-in APIs and explain how you compare elements. SMTS rounds argued about comparator syntax in C++.
dsa.evidence: Broadcom SWE Apr 2024 (merge vs quick, AVL); Broadcom intern Bengaluru Feb 2024 (merge sort); GFG 2023 (quicksort); Sr MTS 2020 round 1; MTS-1 on-campus 2021; SMTS Nov 2023 comparator

dsa.title: Concurrency coding drills: two-thread lock, reader-writer, producer-consumer, ping-pong tasks
dsa.statement: Recurring coded exercises: (a) design a lock with acquire()/release() used by two threads and write it (also 'mutual exclusion without kernel primitives' — Peterson/Dekker or atomics); (b) multithreaded reader-writer problem in C++ with variations (writer preference, condition variables); (c) bounded producer-consumer queue with mutex + condition variables, and why volatile does not fix data races; (d) two asynchronous tasks that alternately hand control to each other (C#/Java async), and converting a synchronous routine to asynchronous; (e) write a multithreaded program touching shared global data and list the precautions.
dsa.evidence: Sr MTS Apr 2020 rounds 1-2; Sr MTS Oct 2020 round 3; MTS-3 Bengaluru Jun 2021; VMware MTS phone 2017 (producer-consumer); Broadcom Glassdoor Jan 2026 (queue + producer-consumer, via PracHub)

dsa.title: Python file-processing assignment with modular classes (live, ~45 min)
dsa.statement: Read a large text file, extract all digits and arrange them into an N x N matrix, validate the matrix is correctly ordered, transpose it, and emit a list of dictionaries. Interviewer required modular, edge-case-safe code and asked for a split into a custom Exception class, a FileReader, a Configuration holder and a main driver; followed by TCP vs UDP and HTTP vs HTTPS.
dsa.variant: A similar 'read a list from an API, extract a field, sort and return strings' task appeared in a Java MTS-1 loop.
dsa.evidence: VMware MTS-2 round 2 (LeetCode Discuss); MTS-1 off-campus 2021 round 1

dsa.title: Debug a C++ program that compiles but produces wrong output
dsa.statement: A dedicated debugging round: you are shown a syntactically valid C++ program whose output is wrong and must find and fix the flaw (typical culprits: off-by-one, integer overflow, dangling reference, copy vs reference, uninitialised member, operator precedence). Preceded by a discussion of your debugging habits and tools (GDB/WinDbg, sanitizers, logging).
dsa.variant: Java variant: 'debug this Java code' rapid-fire in a 2021 campus loop; 'improve an existing piece of code' (sync -> async) for a C# team.
dsa.evidence: VMware MTS-2 Pune 2024 round 4; MTS-3 Feb 2022 scenario round (GDB); MTS-1 on-campus 2021

dsa.title: CS fundamentals: processes vs threads, fork(), zombie/orphan, context switch
dsa.statement: Explain what happens on fork() (copy-on-write address space, return values, what is shared), how threads differ from processes (shared heap/code vs private stack/registers, cost of creation and context switch), what a zombie and an orphan process are and how to avoid them, what a context switch saves/restores and why process->kernel context differs from process->process. Expect 'how do threads communicate and in what modes do they run' and 'extends Thread vs implements Runnable' in Java rounds.
dsa.evidence: Sr MTS Apr 2020 round 1; Intern+MTS 2021 round 1; Sr MTS Oct 2020 round 2; MTS-3 Dec 2020 round 1 (threads, processes); Interview Query Symantec reports

dsa.title: CS fundamentals: virtual memory, paging, page faults, TLB, malloc path, thrashing
dsa.statement: Walk through what happens in user space vs kernel on malloc(4) (brk/mmap, allocator arenas, lazy physical backing, can malloc fail?), whether the returned address is virtual or physical, the page-table walk and why the TLB exists, what a page fault is and how it is handled (minor vs major), virtual memory layout of a process, thrashing, the memory hierarchy (registers/cache/RAM) and how data moves from RAM to registers, memory leaks and segmentation. Also 'stack vs heap' as a 1-minute answer.
dsa.evidence: Sr MTS Apr 2020 round 1; GFG 2023 technical round (paging, page fault, virtual memory); Intern+MTS 2021 (thrashing, memory leaks); MTS2 Jan 2023 (stack vs heap)

dsa.title: CS fundamentals: mutex vs semaphore vs spinlock, mutex internals, deadlock and mitigation
dsa.statement: Define synchronization and critical sections; contrast mutex (ownership, sleeping), binary/counting semaphore (signalling, no ownership) and spinlock (busy-wait, when it wins); explain how a mutex is implemented internally (atomic test-and-set/CAS + futex-style wait queue) and critical-section APIs in C++ (std::mutex, lock_guard, condition_variable) and in Windows kernel mode; give a concrete deadlock example and the four conditions, then mitigation (lock ordering, try-lock with backoff, timeouts, lock hierarchy) and detection. Be ready to write deadlock-producing code on a whiteboard and then fix it.
dsa.evidence: MTS-3 Feb 2022 design round (deadlock, spinlock/mutex/semaphore, context switching); SMTS Bengaluru Jul 2024 rounds 1-2 (mutex internals, critical sections); Sr MTS Apr 2020; GFG on-campus (deadlock code); Broadcom Staff 2013 (semaphore vs mutex)

dsa.title: CS fundamentals: system calls, user/kernel boundary, interrupts, file-system call path
dsa.statement: Explain how a system call works end to end using open() (trap, syscall table, VFS lookup, file descriptor), how the OS decides which file system implements the call (mount table, superblock ops) and what mount() does internally; interrupts and processing in kernel context; how user mode communicates with kernel mode and vice versa (ioctl, syscalls, signals, shared memory / on Windows IRPs). Windows-kernel teams add paged vs non-paged pool, critical sections in kernel mode and debugging a crash dump in WinDbg. Broadcom storage teams ask 'describe the I/O path of a file save'.
dsa.evidence: Sr MTS Apr 2020 round 2 (open(), mount()); SMTS Bengaluru Jul 2024 round 3 (kernel/user communication, pools, WinDbg); Broadcom Sr SWE storage (I/O path of file save, Glassdoor 2026)

dsa.title: CS fundamentals: networking — TCP vs UDP, handshake, HTTP vs HTTPS, OSI, DNS/DHCP, URL-to-page
dsa.statement: Standard set asked after a coding problem: TCP vs UDP (3-way handshake, reliability, ordering, congestion control, when to pick UDP), HTTP vs HTTPS (TLS handshake, certificates), the OSI layers and which protocols sit at L3/L4, DNS resolution and DHCP, private vs public IPs and how a router/NAT assigns addresses (including two PCs joined by one Ethernet cable — link-local/APIPA), and 'what happens when you type a URL in the browser'. NSX/Brocade teams go deeper (routing protocols, L2/L3 in software vs hardware, Kubernetes networking).
dsa.evidence: GFG 2023 technical round (OSI, TCP vs UDP); MTS-2 round 2 (TCP/UDP, HTTP/HTTPS) and HLD round (L3/L4); Intern+MTS 2021 (DNS, DHCP, IP assignment, URL in browser); Broadcom Bengaluru AWS cloud engineer 2022-2026 (K8s networking)

dsa.title: CS fundamentals: C++ internals — virtual functions/vptr, diamond problem, pointers, name mangling, extern "C", copies
dsa.statement: What a virtual function is and how the runtime reaches the derived implementation (vptr/vtable laid out per object, virtual destructor rules); the diamond problem and virtual inheritance; types of pointers (raw, unique/shared/weak, dangling, void, function) and when to use each; constructors/destructors order, RAII; private vs protected vs public and friend; name mangling and why extern "C" exists; deep vs shallow copy and the rule of three/five; how std::vector, std::list and a hash table are implemented and the cost of traversing a list vs an array (cache locality). Interviewers ask these as confusing follow-ups to test confidence.
dsa.evidence: MTS-2 Pune 2024 rounds 1-3; SMTS Bengaluru Jul 2024 round 2; MTS-1 2022 round 3; MTS-3 Feb 2022 round 3; MTS2 Jan 2023 round 1; Sr MTS Oct 2020 (deep vs shallow copy)

dsa.title: CS fundamentals: Java concurrency and collections internals (control-plane / Symantec teams)
dsa.statement: How ConcurrentHashMap achieves concurrency (bucket-level CAS/synchronized bins) vs Hashtable; what ConcurrentModificationException is; how BlockingQueue blocks producers/consumers when full/empty; extends Thread vs implements Runnable; how synchronization is achieved (synchronized, locks, volatile); wait/notify; Streams API; wrapper classes and collections; garbage collection; serialization; final/static/abstract; write an immutable class; expose a List via a getter that callers cannot mutate (unmodifiable view, defensive copy) and how that changes for a String[].
dsa.evidence: Sr MTS Oct 2020 round 2; MTS2 Bangalore Apr 2022 HM screen and round 5; MTS-1 off-campus 2021; on-campus 2022 (GC, multithreading, serialization); Broadcom Hyderabad Jun 2023 (core Java, Kafka, microservices)

dsa.title: CS fundamentals: databases — ACID, indexes and their cost, read- vs write-heavy stores, sharding, replication
dsa.statement: ACID with a deep dive on durability (WAL, fsync) and an example; how indexes work (B-tree) and their drawbacks (write amplification, storage); query optimisation basics; choosing read-heavy vs write-heavy databases with use cases; can a relational DB scale horizontally — sharding strategies applied to your own project's schema, master-slave replication and failover; MySQL vs PostgreSQL differences; a few PostgreSQL commands; SQL/DBMS MCQs in OAs.
dsa.evidence: MTS-2 HLD round (LeetCode Discuss); on-campus 2021 (ACID durability); MTS2 Jan 2023 round 2 (master-slave); MTS-3 Jun 2021 HM round (database design)

dsa.title: CS fundamentals: tooling — Git merge vs rebase, Linux CLI, Docker/Kubernetes, GDB, CI/CD
dsa.statement: Rapid-fire practical questions: how Git works and merge vs rebase; pipe, su vs sudo, write a CLI file search with grep; Docker and Kubernetes experience (installation, day-2 operations, troubleshooting, storage and networking for K8s on cloud-engineer loops); debugging a running service with GDB; log levels and reconstructing an incident from logs; testing types (unit, smoke, black/white box) and what makes code production-ready; Jenkins/CI-CD; macOS/Linux/Windows familiarity.
dsa.evidence: MTS-2 HLD round (Git, Docker/K8s); MTS-1 on-campus 2021 round 2-3; MTS-3 Feb 2022 scenario round (GDB, logs); MTS-3 Dec 2020 (Jenkins, Docker); Broadcom Bengaluru AWS cloud engineer (K8s day-2 ops, Glassdoor 2026)
